section_summary.extract_value: This section reports test–retest reliability for BAS-2 scores in separate female and male samples: females (n = 57) showed an intraclass correlation of .82 (CI = .59–.86) and males (n = 52) showed an intraclass correlation of .87 (CI = .78–.93). Mean BAS-2 scores did not differ significantly between the first and second testing sessions for either females (M1 = 3.90, M2 = 4.02, p = .188) or males (M1 = 3.78, M2 = 3.74, p = .654). No study numbering or additional sample details (e.g., country, age, BMI) are provided in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: Sentences: 'For the test–retest female sample (n = 57), the intraclass correlation coefficient between the BAS-2 scores at the first and second testing sessions 3 weeks apart was .82 (CI = .59–.86). Mean scores were not significantly different across the first (M = 3.90, SD = 0.71) and second testing sessions (M = 4.02, SD = 0.81), t(56) = 1.33, p = .188.' and 'In men (n = 52), the intraclass correlation coefficient between the BAS-2 scores at the two testing sessions was .87 (CI = .78–.93). Mean scores were not significantly different across the first (M = 3.78, SD = 0.76) and second testing sessions (M = 3.74, SD = 0.81), t(51) = 0.45, p = .654.'
